gate.how: node --experimental-strip-types with registerHooks, importing gateSense directly; every row passed through it on both passes
gate.result: pass 1: 63/66 ok, 3 rejected. one repair round applied. pass 2: 66/66 ok, 0 rejected, 0 discarded.
gate.pre_write_check: Rule A'1: 120 candidate content words were checked against allowed-words BEFORE drafting, which rejected in advance: soup, powder, melt, melting, alphabet, savings, litre, lamp, bench, boil, purple, bare, cloth, airport, queen, nephew, niece. Lesson 9 says the check must run on the FINAL text, not on a candidate list - it was run on the full drafted file too, and the three words it still missed (two x2, wrist) were born while phrasing, exactly as lesson 9 predicts.
gate.post_gate_check: Every stem was scanned for a plural-forcing quantifier immediately before the blank (lesson 8): 0 hits. Distractor mix verified 2 semantic / 1 orthographic / 1 unrelated on all 66 rows. Every distractor was substituted into all three of its own stems before writing (lessons 6-7); antonyms were excluded by rule, which is why finish/start, sit/stand, rise/fall and top/base do not appear as distractors of one another.
